title: Consecutive reduction for normalized integral scalar pullback maps
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E,L/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite extensions and $\iota:E\to L$ an embedding. Use the specified ordinary scalar-extension functors $S_W$ [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension] and finite operation functors [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined]. For a scheme map $f:X\to Y$, let $P^E_n,P^L_n$ be the specified finite pullback functors, with their recorded consecutive transitions $r^E_n,r^L_n$. Suppose $\alpha_n:S_X P^E_n\to P^L_n S_Y$ are natural chain maps sending each local generator $1\otimes f^*(1\otimes x)$ to $f^*(1\otimes(1\otimes x))$ over the base-changed object. Then for every $n$, $S_X(r^E_n);\alpha_n=\alpha_{n+1};r^L_n S_Y$. This is only the consecutive reduction equation; it asserts neither existence nor uniqueness of a map on whole towers.

source.place: Section tensor-product, including lemma-sheafification-tensor and lemma-tensor-product-pullback; finite quotient transition argument in Bhatt--Scholze Definition 3.4.10 and Stacks 07A4.

proof.text: The completed projection to each finite quotient is locally surjective. Compose the E consecutive quotient map with the E-to-L finite coefficient map. The limit projection relation and normalization of the completed scalar map show that this composite after the E projection equals the completed scalar map followed by the L projection.

In each degree transpose the two maps through the ordinary scalar-extension adjunction. Local surjectivity of the E completed projection lifts their resulting completed-linear maps to finite-linear maps into restriction along the finite E-to-L coefficient map. Transpose through the finite pullback adjunction. Equality is then tested on unit pure tensors by the finite scalar-extension universal property. The three unit formulas identify the test sections with precisely the displayed normalized generators.

The recorded pullback transition sends a pullback generator to the generator of its reduced input. The finite quotient transition sends 1 tensor x to 1 tensor x. Naturality of the ordinary scalar tensor unit and the two assumed normalizations therefore make both composites equal to the level-n pullback generator of 1 tensor (1 tensor x). Apply the preceding extensionality argument, then chain-map and natural-transformation extensionality.

proof_origin.note: Use the underived adjunctions and existing private finite-linearity and tensor-extensionality APIs; no derived coefficient adjunction and no split-off obligations.

lean.statement:
theorem integralScalarPullbackLevelReduction {X Y : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (α : ∀ n : ℕ, integralOperationsPullbackLevel l E f n ⋙
        (integralOrdinaryScalar l E L ι X).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⟶
      (integralOrdinaryScalar l E L ι Y).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
        integralOperationsPullbackLevel l L f n)
    (hα : ∀ (n : ℕ) (P : CochainComplex (integralTowerModules l E Y) ℤ) (i : ℤ) (V : Y.ProEt)
        (x : (P.X i).val.obj (op V)),
        (((α n).app P).f i).val.app (op ((AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.proEtaleBaseChange f).obj V))
          (integralOrdinaryTensorSection l E L ι X
            (((integralOperationsPullbackLevel l E f n).obj P).X i)
            (op ((AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.proEtaleBaseChange f).obj V)) 1
            (integralOperationsPullbackGenerator l E f n
              (((unrestrictedIntegralFiniteComplex l E Y n).obj P).X i) V
              (unrestrictedIntegralTensorSection l E Y n (P.X i) (op V) 1 x))) =
        integralOperationsPullbackGenerator l L f n
          (((unrestrictedIntegralFiniteComplex l L Y n).obj
            (((integralOrdinaryScalar l E L ι Y).mapHomologicalComplex
              (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj P)).X i) V
          (unrestrictedIntegralTensorSection l L Y n
            ((integralOrdinaryScalar l E L ι Y).obj (P.X i)) (op V) 1
            (integralOrdinaryTensorSection l E L ι Y (P.X i) (op V) 1 x))) (n : ℕ) :
    Functor.whiskerRight (integralOperationsPullbackTransition l E f n)
        ((integralOrdinaryScalar l E L ι X).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) ≫
      α n =
    α (n + 1) ≫ Functor.whiskerLeft
      ((integralOrdinaryScalar l E L ι Y).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
      (integralOperationsPullbackTransition l L f n)
